rounds.text: Ranjit Securities Ltd presents a significant valuation disconnect, trading at a P/E ratio of 112x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 60.99x, which vastly exceeds the sector benchmarks of 17.93x and 12.98x respectively [E6, E11]. This premium pricing is fundamentally unsupported by the company's performance, as evidenced by a compounded profit growth rate that has plummeted by 64% over the trailing twelve months [E21] and a consistent long-term decline in profit growth [E18, E19, E20]. The market is currently pricing in an aggressive 32.1% earnings growth expectation, a figure that stands in stark contrast to the company's actual low returns on equity [E25, E34]. Furthermore, the cash conversion ratio of 0.57x indicates that reported profits are not being effectively translated into actual cash flow [E26]. Conceded: the company is almost debt-free [E38] and has demonstrated recent sales growth [E17]. Despite these factors, the intrinsic value derived from a discounted cash flow analysis suggests the current market price is detached from reality, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -685.0% [E32, E33].
